## Requirement

Requester: Acme Software, B2B support team. Today support runs from a shared mailbox.

## Scope

### In scope

- Case data model: two record types (Support, Billing) with their Support Processes as files of their own, the Email-Support / Email-Billing / Web Origin values DEFINED by standardValueSets/CaseOrigin.standardValueSet-meta.xml, the Case compact layout and its assignment, and the Account fields the routing and SLA layers read (Region__c, Support_Tier__c) [Q1, Q2, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q19, Q83, Q85]
- Page layouts per Case record type, with 'Assign using active assignment rule' defaulted on for manual entry [Q3, Q24, Q83] — the compact layout sits with the object model in M1-S01, not here
- Access model: a minimal base profile per team over permission set groups for Tier 1, Tier 2 and Billing, covering Case, Account, Contact, EmailMessage, Entitlement and the Service app [Q3, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10, Q11, Q12, Q86, Q87]
- An intake-bypass Custom Permission on an integration permission set, so API-created cases are never blocked by a rule aimed at agents [Q56]
- Three Case queues (Tier 1 General, Tier 2 Engineering, Billing) with role-and-public-group membership and no named users [Q26, Q29, Q30, Q88, Q89]
- Case org-wide default Private plus a criteria-based sharing rule opening Support cases to Tier 2; nothing opens Billing cases to Tier 1 [Q13 (deferred, conservative reading), Q80]
- Case validation rules with the intake bypass, component-field formulas and final message text written at design time [Q5, Q56, Q58, Q59, Q93]
- Email-to-Case for support@acme.example and billing@acme.example with per-address Origin stamping, bounce-on-unauthorised-sender, requeue-on-over-limit and saveEmailHeaders on [Q15, Q17, Q18, Q19, Q21, Q23, Q74]
- Web-to-Case intake for the website form at ~60 submissions a day: the CaseSettings.webToCase block (enableWebToCase, caseOrigin) in the same physical settings/Case.settings-meta.xml as the Email-to-Case block. The HTML form itself is not metadata and is authored outside this build [Q15, Q66]
- Case assignment rules routing on Origin and account support tier with a Tier 1 General catch-all, plus auto-response rules [Q24, Q25, Q26, Q27]
- Classic acknowledgement and escalation email templates sent from support@ and billing@ as verified org-wide addresses, carrying the case number and the thread token [Q22, Q28, Q60, Q61, Q62, Q63, Q64, Q78]
- Queue-based Omni-Channel push for Tier 1 is the chosen mechanism (D4, automation-selection Q13) but its configuration is BLOCKED on deferred Q32-Q35; only the pull surface ships in this phase, and Tier 1 works the Tier 1 General queue list view in the interim [Q31, Q36, Q37]
- Business Hours for EMEA (London 08:00-18:00), the US (New York 08:00-20:00, org default) and a 24/7 Severity 1 calendar, plus regional holidays and a named yearly maintenance owner [Q38, Q39, Q40, Q90]
- Entitlement process for Premier (4 business hours) and Standard (1 business day) over one shared First Response milestone type, with the Case's calendar as the explicit authority, plus the after-update Apex trigger that writes CaseMilestone.CompletionDate so the milestone can actually close [Q38, Q50, Q51, Q53]
- A before-save record-triggered Flow stamping EntitlementId, BusinessHoursId and the Priority default, with a documented no-matching-account fallback [Q16, Q40, Q48]
- Case escalation rules: an 8-business-hour Tier 2 entry on the Case calendar (480 minutes, from CaseCreation) and a 24/7 Severity 1 entry, both deployed inactive [Q42, Q43, Q44, Q45, Q46, Q47, Q91]
- Pull list views for Tier 2 and Billing plus a saved report on escalated, still-open Cases in a shared folder [Q31, Q91]
- A sandbox proof: Partial Copy object selection (Account, Contact, Case, Entitlement, EmailMessage) and post-refresh re-pointing of the routing addresses and the form endpoint — BLOCKED. sandbox-strategy-designer requires team_size, concurrent_workstreams, release_cadence and data_sensitivity for a design run and refuses without team size or cadence; none of the four is in requirement.md, in the 97 clarifications, or in a depends_on step's outputs [Q68, Q72, Q74, Q76]
- Documentation, all of it from build-doc-keeper's compile run except the backlog: the ten-section configuration workbook, the traceability matrix, the compiled deploy order, the UAT test-case pack (uat-test-cases.yaml) and the compiled acceptance-criteria document; the INVEST story backlog with its per-story criteria from story-drafter; and the build-level package.xml and deploy-order note from metadata-builder [Q77, Q80, Q84, Q87, Q89, Q90, Q94, Q96, Q97]

### Out of scope

- Phone / telephony, chat, knowledge base and customer portal — named out of scope by the requirement itself and reinforced by Q30 (Case is the only queue-supported object) and Q12 (employees only)
- Skills-based Omni-Channel routing — descoped by Q37: the requirement describes three team queues and no skill dimension
- Person Accounts — descoped by Q6: Acme is B2B, so Cases hang off Business Accounts and Contacts
- Lead routing, Lead queues and lead-convert ownership — descoped by Q30: no Lead work item is described
- Migration of historical cases from the shared mailbox — descoped by Q4 and Q58: no Salesforce Case records exist and none are being loaded
- Field-level masking of billing data on a shared Case record — blocked on deferred Q13; the plan takes the record-level reading instead (assumption A1) and this alternative shape is out until Q13 is answered
- An elapsed-working-time field for reports or code — blocked on deferred Q41 (assumption A8)
- Milestone clock stop / pause (isStopped) and who may stop it — blocked on deferred Q52 (assumption A10)
- Entitlement versioning and its owner — blocked on deferred Q92 (assumption A24)
- A milestone end-condition other than case closure — blocked on deferred Q49 (assumption A9)
- The sandbox ladder itself: allocation, refresh floors, which environments hold copied production records, and post-copy automation — blocked on deferred Q69, Q70, Q71, Q73 and Q75 (assumptions A17-A21). Only the single proof sandbox from Q68 and Q72 is planned
- Test-data creation mechanism (UI vs Data Loader vs Bulk API vs REST) — blocked on deferred Q79 (assumption A22)
- The reporting backlog beyond the escalation monitoring report — blocked on deferred Q65 (assumption A14)
- An as-is process map of what the support team does today — blocked on deferred Q67 (assumption A16)
- Per-expected-result evidence design and the deny-case pre-condition audit — blocked on deferred Q81 and Q82 (assumptions A23 and A15); the UAT pack build-doc-keeper compiles in M5-S04 carries placeholders a human closes
- A defined rule for what must NOT happen automatically, and who repairs a wrong automation — blocked on deferred Q14 (assumption A2). Until it is answered the stamping flow writes only into null fields
- Deployment to any org — out of scope for this layer by contract: the plan produces deploy-ready artefacts, a deploy order and a validate-only command, and a human deploys
- Omni-Channel configuration itself — the objects pushed and capacity release, the agent capacity model and per-case weight, the routing model and tie-breaker, and the push-timeout behaviour — blocked on deferred Q32, Q33, Q34 and Q35 (assumptions A4-A7). M3-S05 is written blocked rather than shipping invented numbers; D4 records the mechanism the tree does settle
- Milestone violation polling and any scheduled SLA sweep — the library's mechanism (skills/apex/entitlement-apex-hooks MilestoneViolationScheduler) is Schedulable, which D8 rules out for this phase; M4-S05 builds completion only
- The sandbox proof plan document itself — BLOCKED, not descoped: sandbox-strategy-designer's four design-mandatory inputs (team_size, concurrent_workstreams, release_cadence, data_sensitivity) exist nowhere on file, so M5-S02 is written blocked rather than handed a partial map. Closing them is a clarification round, not a re-plan of this build.
- A mechanical checker on M2-S04's queues and M3-S04's assignment rules — two library checkers cannot pass on this build's correct artefacts (check_queues.py fails any queue with no queueEmail, which Q88 requires of Tier 1 General; check_assignment_rules.py fails a target named by more than one entry, which Q18 plus Q26 require). Those assertions are carried by manual tests and the findings are recorded as deepen-a-skill signals rather than worked around. W02 (v4 verification): the third checker named here in v4 — check_case_management_setup.py, said to read <active> as a direct child of <AssignmentRules> — is REPAIRED and is no longer scoped out. rule_elements (:78-90) now reads <active> and <ruleEntry> from the inner <assignmentRule> element and find_xml_files (:62-76) recurses into every assignmentRules/ directory at any depth, so the milestone case-management sweep is back in scope: it is declared on M3-S03, on M3-S04 and as M3's own milestone test, all at --manifest-dir artefacts, and all three were re-run on a fixture before being declared.

## Decisions

| Id | Decision | Decision tree | Branch | ADR | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `D1` | Stamp Case.EntitlementId, Case.BusinessHoursId and the Priority default in one before-save record-triggered Flow rather than in Apex or an after-save Flow. | `standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md` | Q2 |  | All three writes land on the triggering Case and the Account/Entitlement reads are lookups, not DML, so Q1's record-change branch reaches Q2. Q2's first branch redirects the Case-specific engine choices to Q13, and this plan takes that redirect elsewhere: the owner write is D3 (Q13), the acknowledgement is the auto-response rule in M3-S04 (Q13), and the SLA engine itself is the entitlement process in M4-S02 (Q15). What is left at Q2's plain 'Yes' leaf is exactly this step — the same-record field write that puts the Case into that engine. The Q15 leaf note is why the step has to exist at all: 'neither Email-to-Case nor Web-to-Case supplies an entitlement, so a case-intake design that stops at the channel tracks nothing until something assigns one.' |
| `D2` | The stamping flow is before-save, not after-save: the Account and Entitlement lookups are read-only Get Records, which a before-save flow supports. | `standards/decision-trees/flow-pattern-selector.md` | Q3 |  | Q1 'record INSERT or UPDATE' → Q2 'only set fields on the SAME record' → Q3 'no DML, no action, no email' → before-save. The branch text settles the one thing that looked like an obstacle: the cross-object read is allowed. |

It does: D3 takes the first leaf (the first owner comes from an ordered criteria table of field values -> Assignment Rules) for the initial owner write, and this decision takes the second (the record is already in a queue and must reach whichever agent is online and under capacity -> Omni-Channel) for the push. - `D1`
  - Branch quote: Q2. Does the logic run in under ~10s and touch only fields on the record itself? ├── Yes, but the field is OwnerId (or an acknowledgement, or an SLA │ clock) on a Case or a Lead → Q13 ├── Yes → Before-save record-triggered Flow └── No → Q3
  - Alternatives rejected: Apex before-insert trigger; After-save record-triggered Flow; three separate flows, one per field
  - Consequences: No Apex means no coverage gate and no deploy-time test dependency, but also no custom exception handling: a Case whose Account has no entitlement must fall through to a documented default rather than throw (Q48).
- `D2`
  - Branch quote: Q3. Do you need any DML, an Action/callout, or an email — anything beyond writing fields on the triggering record? ├── No → Before-Save record-triggered flow. Its element set is Assignment, Decision, Get Records, Loop — so a read-only cross-object lookup is fine here; a write is not.
  - Alternatives rejected: After-save record-triggered flow; After-save with a scheduled path
  - Consequences: The customer acknowledgement (an email) cannot live in this flow; it stays in the auto-response rule (M3-S04), which is what Q63 asked for anyway.
- `D3`
  - Branch quote: Q13. Which native rule engine on Case or Lead owns this write? ├── The first owner comes from an ordered criteria table │ of field values → Assignment Rules · `admin/assignment-rules`
  - Source reference: `skills/admin/assignment-rules/references/routing-selector.md`
  - Alternatives rejected: Before-save record-triggered Flow setting OwnerId; Apex trigger with round-robin counter; Omni-Channel alone with no queue-landing rule
  - Consequences: Two by-design post-save OwnerId writers remain (Omni-Channel push in M3-S05 and the escalation rule in M4-S04). Q27 already flagged this; owner-writer-map.md in M3-S04 is the artefact that has to reconcile all three.
- `D4`
  - Branch quote: Q13. Which native rule engine on Case or Lead owns this write? ├── The first owner comes from an ordered criteria table │ of field values → Assignment Rules · `admin/assignment-rules` ├── The record is already in a queue and must reach whichever │ agent is online and under capacity → Omni-Channel · `admin/omni-channel-routing-setup` ├── The submitter must be acknowledged by email as the │ record is created → Auto-Response Rules · `admin/assignment-rules` ├── The record arrives from an inbound intake channel → Q14 ├── Something must happen because time has passed → Q15 └── Not Case or Lead, or the criteria need code → Q3
  - Source reference: `skills/admin/assignment-rules/references/routing-selector.md`
  - Alternatives rejected: Skills-based routing (Q37: no skill dimension in the requirement); Per-user presence assignment (Q36: Tier 1 membership changes monthly); Apex round-robin (ignores presence and capacity)
  - Consequences: Omni-Channel writes OwnerId after save, which is the second of the three owner writers D3 has to reconcile. M3-S05 is blocked on Q32-Q35, so nothing in this build configures the push half; Tier 1 works the Tier 1 General queue list view produced by M5-S01 until those four questions are answered.
- `D5`
  - Branch quote: Q3. Can the access be described by "anyone who matches criteria X should see records matching criteria Y"? ├── Yes, criteria are on the record itself → Criteria-Based Sharing Rule
  - Alternatives rejected: Public Read-Only OWD; Role-hierarchy grant; Case Teams; Manual sharing; Apex managed sharing
  - Consequences: Deferred Q13 asked whether the Billing restriction is record-level or field-level. The plan takes the record-level (more restrictive) reading as assumption A1. If the answer turns out to be field-level masking, M2-S05 is re-planned, not patched.
- `D6`
  - Branch quote: Q14. Which intake channel creates the Case? ├── Customer email to a monitored routing address → Email-to-Case · `admin/email-to-case-configuration` ├── An HTML form posted from a public website → Web-to-Case · `admin/case-management-setup`
  - Alternatives rejected: Bulk API 2.0; Middleware / iPaaS; Custom @RestResource endpoint
  - Consequences: Q66 left open whether the form posts directly or through middleware. If middleware turns out to sit in front, the Origin stamping in M3-S03 and the assignment criteria in M3-S04 both change. Assumption A26 is not recorded because Q66 is answered — the answer itself says 'confirm', so the confirmation is a manual test on M3-S03.
- `D7`
  - Branch quote: Q15. What does the passage of time have to do? ├── Re-route or notify when an open Case ages past a │ threshold → Escalation Rules · `admin/escalation-rules`
  - Source reference: `skills/admin/assignment-rules/references/routing-selector.md`
  - Alternatives rejected: Schedule-triggered Flow polling open Cases; After-save Flow with a scheduled path; Batch Apex
  - Consequences: The escalation engine batches, so the 480-minute threshold is not a to-the-second promise (Q46 asked for headroom to be agreed). The rule also writes OwnerId, which is the third owner writer D3 has to reconcile.
- `D8`
  - Branch quote: Q1. How many records / how long? ├── < 2,000 records, < 60s → Q2 ├── 2k – 50k, < 5 min → Q5 (Queueable) ├── > 50k OR > 5 min → Q8 (Batch Apex) └── Truly massive, one-off ETL → Bulk API 2.0 (async SOQL / external job)
  - Alternatives rejected: Queueable entitlement stamping; Batch Apex nightly SLA sweep; Platform Event fan-out to Tier 2
  - Consequences: Every automation in the plan runs inside the creating transaction, so the before-save flow in M4-S03 is on the critical path of every intake. If volume grows past the Q1 first band, this decision is the one to revisit.
- `D9`
  - Branch quote: Q10. What stage of LDV are you in? ├── Designing a new high-volume object → architect/large-data-volume-architecture (skinny + indexes from day one)
  - Alternatives rejected: Skinny table on Case from day one; Custom index request on Origin; Big Object archival of closed cases
  - Consequences: The escalation monitoring report (M5-S01) and the queue list views (M5-S01) are unindexed selective queries today. Q76 already asked which acceptance criteria depend on volume; if the report degrades, this decision is where the revisit starts.
- `D10`
  - Source reference: `skills/apex/entitlement-apex-hooks/SKILL.md`
  - Alternatives rejected: Satisfiable completion criteria on the entitlement process (no completion-criteria element is documented in the skill's metadata reference); A record-triggered Flow stamping CompletionDate directly (metadata-examples § 9 documents the Flow path as an invocable wrapper around this same Apex, so it adds a component without removing the Apex); Leaving completion manual (gotcha 8: every first-response milestone then reports violated on cases the agent demonstrably answered)
  - Consequences: This is the only Apex in the build, so M4-S05 is the only step under the 75% coverage gate and the only one whose artefacts a deploy will compile. Violation polling is deliberately not built: the same skill's MilestoneViolationScheduler is Schedulable, which D8 rules out for this phase.
